A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CLI framework. All 20 pages of v1 and 33 pages of v2, including Appendices A-F, provide readable text, equations, tables, and figures that support reliable matching and comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of CLI on LLaVA-OneVision and LLaVA-1.5, component and injection-density ablations, data-volume experiments, and qualitative results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds a parameter-matched architecture comparison, an AGF query-source ablation, and computational-cost measurements.

M1.justification: CLI retains the same LoRA-based AMP, attention-based sigmoid gating, masked feature injection, and layer-stride configurations. Appendix E.4 identifies visual-token conditioning as the existing design and tests a text-conditioned alternative; it does not document replacing the proposed method.

E1.justification: Training-data composition and evaluated task coverage remain unchanged. The headline count changes from 18 to 28, but OCR and the nine grounding evaluations already appear in v1 Figure 4. The new controls use retained benchmarks.

E2.justification: v2 adds a static Parallel comparator with a reportedly comparable parameter count in Section 4.3 and Figure 6. Existing benchmark tables retain their comparator sets. Newly discussed CogVLM, CogAgent, and DEHVF are not added to the reported empirical comparisons.

E3.justification: SLI's reported visual-layer selection changes from the first n layers to layers sampled at stride eight. New analyses introduce parameter matching, visual-versus-text conditioning controls, and per-sample MMBench cost measurements. The retained training and benchmark protocols otherwise match; the revised SLI description does not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 substantially extends design validation with a parameter-matched static-fusion control, an AGF query-source ablation, and computational-efficiency analysis. Existing component, data-volume, and injection-density ablations remain. Appendix F's qualitative cases and limitations discussion are retained rather than newly added.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The additional experiments continue reporting single scores without uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantive architecture-control, query-source, and resource-cost results: Table 10 reports Text/Vision totals of 641.18/646.50, and Table 5 reports baseline/CLI inference times of 0.66/0.77 seconds. Existing main-table scores remain unchanged, but Table 2 corrects DeepStack's MathVerse delta from -3.8 to +0.1. Appendix D corrects SLI's reasoning-total decline from 28.6 to 17.6 points and replaces the erroneous MMMU-loss example.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation is retained. v1's two numbered AMP expressions are consolidated into v2 Equation 4, with subsequent renumbering and notation adjustments. No substantive definition, derivation, assumption, theorem, or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion revise the claimed evaluation breadth from 18 to 28 benchmarks, accounting for evaluations already present in v1. A new abstract footnote explicitly limits 'reasoning' to general multimodal inference. The central many-to-many fusion and two-module contribution claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations that visual-query gating enables intramodal residual refinement and avoids a text-induced information bottleneck. It interprets the Parallel control as evidence against a parameter-count explanation and discusses the measured computational tradeoff. Existing qualitative limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 newly supplies a code-repository link and specifies visual-token conditioning as the standard AGF implementation in Appendix E.4. Existing model configurations, LoRA rank and alpha, injection strides, training hyperparameters, and dataset-composition details are retained.

R1.justification: Related work adds CogVLM, CogAgent, a multi-layer fusion study, and concurrent DEHVF, extending comparisons with static fusion designs. The MME citation changes from a survey to the benchmark paper. The overall dynamic-versus-static research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: Most prose and section ordering are retained. Local revisions shorten captions, refine comparator descriptions, rename Section 4.4, add Appendix E.4, standardize module terminology, and update affiliations, correspondence information, and acknowledgements.

P2.justification: The entire document changes from two columns to a narrower single-column layout with running headers, extensively resizing and relocating displays. v2 adds a performance-delta summary, a Parallel-comparison radar plot, and cost and query-source tables. Earlier figures and tables are retained with renumbering.

improvement.justification: The new architecture and query controls, measured computational costs, code-access statement, and numerical corrections make CLI's design and tradeoffs more assessable than in v1. The gain is limited by incomplete configuration details for the added analyses and overstated interpretation: Appendix E.4 claims consistent visual-query superiority, although Table 10 favors text queries on three tasks. Overall, the additions provide useful but qualified improvements to the supporting evidence.
